items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Everything was about Mozart, Tchaikovsky, Beethoven, Bach.

ctx.x: Oh well I didn’t get that far thanks God. But my favorite violin concerto is Tchaikovsky. Tchaikovsky, Mendelssohn, those are my two favorite. But I didn’t get that far. But one thing though, the musical training information in Cuba for many years, even after I left in
1980, was strictly classical. Everything was about Mozart, Tchaikovsky, Beethoven, Bach. Nothing about Afro-Cuban music or Cuban music in general.

So the analogy that occurs to me in the United States about the time you were a teenager would have been rock music, that would have been the popular music for the most part that jazz had been really popular but sort of displanted by rock music. So what was the popular music in Cuba, like when you were let’s say seventeen?
